mainTopic: Folk remedies and spoken formulas, princes wearing bells, and the line between real healing and דרכי האמורי
overview: This amud finishes a long list of folk remedies that belongs to the larger discussion of what a person may wear or carry on שבת. It gives an amulet for a fever that comes every third day. It then gives רבי יוחנן's remedy for a burning fever: cutting a bush over three days while saying the פסוקים about the burning bush (סנה). רב אחא בריה דרבא rearranges those פסוקים so the remedy ends with 'Do not come close.' Next come spoken formulas for boils, for a wound, against a demon, and against the demon of the bathroom. The גמרא then returns to the משנה's line about princes wearing bells: רבי אושעיא says it follows רבי שמעון, and רבא says the bells are woven into the garment. A new משנה follows, where רבי מאיר permits healing charms on שבת and חכמים forbid them as דרכי האמורי. אביי and רבא rule that anything that truly heals is not דרכי האמורי, and the גמרא shows that marking a tree so people will pray also counts. Finally, רבי חייא בר אבין says the whole Amorite chapter is forbidden except for certain remedies, beginning with formulas for a bone stuck in the throat.

steps.title: Remedy for a fever that comes every third day
steps.stepSummary: The list of remedies continues with an amulet for tertian fever: seven items from each of seven sources, tied to the collar with a hair thread.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a fever that comes every third day, a person should bring seven thorns from seven palm trees, seven slivers from seven beams, seven pegs from seven bridges, seven kinds of ash from seven ovens, seven kinds of dust from seven door-sockets, seven kinds of tar from seven boats, seven cumin seeds, and seven hairs from the beard of an old dog. He should tie them to the neck-opening of his garment with a thread made of hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues a list of fever remedies (taught earlier in the name of אביי's foster mother) and gives the cure for a fever that comes every third day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each fever type gets its own remedy. This one is built on the number seven: seven items, each taken from seven different sources. Everything is worn as an amulet at the collar, tied with a thread of hair.

keyTerms.meaning: Third, here meaning a fever that comes every third day
Door-sockets, the holes the door hinge turns in

steps.whyThisMatters: The larger סוגיא deals with which healing practices are allowed to be worn or carried, and which are forbidden as דרכי האמורי (pagan practices). Remedies like this are treated as legitimate רפואה.

phrases.english: For a tertian fever (every third day) —
let him bring seven thorns from seven palm trees,
and seven slivers from seven beams,
and seven pegs from seven bridges,
and seven ashes from seven ovens,
and seven dusts from seven door-sockets,
and seven tars from seven boats,
and seven cumin seeds,
and seven hairs from the beard of an old dog,
and let him tie them at the opening of the collar
with a thread of hair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of fever remedies from the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For tertian fever, wear seven-from-seven items tied at the collar with a hair thread.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's setup for curing a burning fever
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says to take an all-iron knife, go to a bush, and tie a hair thread to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: For a burning fever, a person should take a knife made entirely of iron, go to a place where there is a bush, and tie a hair thread to it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן begins a new remedy, this time for a burning fever. This step only gives the preparations; the actual daily ritual comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every detail matters here. The knife must be all iron, including the handle. The plant must be a bush, which hints at the burning bush (סנה) that comes up in the next step. A hair thread is tied to it, just like the thread in the previous remedy.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
For a burning fever —
let him take a knife that is entirely iron,
and let him go to where there is a bush,
and tie on it a thread of hair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new fever type and a new authority.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a burning fever: take an all-iron knife, go to a bush, and tie a hair thread to it.

steps.title: The three-day schedule of cutting and reciting
steps.stepSummary: Each day for three days, he cuts the bush a little and says the next פסוק of the burning-bush story in שמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the first day, he cuts the bush a little and says: 'And an angel of ה׳ appeared to him…' The next day, he cuts it a little and says: 'And משה said: I will turn aside now and see.' The next day, he cuts it a little and says: 'And ה׳ saw that he turned aside to see…'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן finishes his remedy. Over three days, you cut the bush a little each day and say one פסוק about the burning bush.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים are the first three in order from the סנה story (שמות ג:ב–ד). In that story the bush burned but was not consumed. Using this story fits a burning fever: the hope is that the person will burn but not be destroyed.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.: the rest of the פסוק is implied

steps.confusionAlert: Each 'וגו׳' means you say the whole פסוק, not just the opening words quoted here.

phrases.english: On the first day, let him cut it a little
and say: 'And an angel of ה׳ appeared to him, etc.'
The next day, let him cut it a little
and say: 'And Moshe said: I will turn aside now and see.'
The next day, let him cut it a little

phrases.aramaic: וְלֵימָא: ״וַיַּרְא ה׳ כִּי סָר לִרְאוֹת וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: and say: 'And ה׳ saw that he turned aside to see, etc.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יוחנן's remedy, which step 2 set up.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For three days, cut the bush a little each day and recite שמות ג:ב, ג:ג, and ג:ד in order.

steps.title: Why leave out 'Do not come close'?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks רב אשי why the remedy doesn't include the next פסוק, 'Do not come close,' which fits a fever best.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, the son of רבא, said to רב אשי: But let him say 'And He said: Do not come close here…'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בריה דרבא challenges the list of פסוקים. He says it skips the most fitting one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The very next פסוק (שמות ג:ה) says 'Do not come close here.' That is the perfect message to tell a fever to stay away. So why would the remedy stop just before it?

keyTerms.meaning: But let him say! (here used as a challenge)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava said to Rav Ashi:
But let him say: 'And He said: Do not come close here, etc.'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי, וְלֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges which פסוקים were chosen in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of three פסוקים in רבי יוחנן's remedy.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The most fitting פסוק, 'Do not come close,' is left out, even though it directly tells the fever to keep away.

steps.title: A revised three-day schedule that includes 'Do not come close'
steps.stepSummary: The first two פסוקים are combined on day one, so that 'Do not come close' can be said on day three.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, on the first day he should say: 'And an angel of ה׳ appeared to him…' together with 'And משה said…'. On the next day he should say: 'And ה׳ saw that he turned aside to see.' And on the next day: 'And ה׳ said: Do not come close here.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בריה דרבא himself goes on to propose a fix. The first two פסוקים are joined on day one, which frees up a slot so 'Do not come close' can be said on the third day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ritual still lasts three days, but now it covers four פסוקים instead of three. The schedule ends on the most powerful one, 'Do not come close.' Only the order changes; the bush, the knife, and the cutting stay the same.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's burning-fever remedy uses the burning-bush פסוקים over three days. According to רב אחא בריה דרבא, day one gets two פסוקים so the remedy can end with 'Do not come close' (שמות ג:ה).

phrases.english: Rather, on the first day, let him say:
'And an angel of ה׳ appeared to him, etc.'
and 'And Moshe said, etc.',

phrases.aramaic: וְלִמְחַר, לֵימָא: ״וַיַּרְא ה׳ כִּי סָר לִרְאוֹת״,
phrases.english: and the next day, let him say: 'And ה׳ saw that he turned aside to see,'
and the next day: 'And ה׳ said: Do not come close here.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge in step 4 by rearranging the schedule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Restructuring: combine two פסוקים on day one to make room for the missing one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Say one פסוק per day for the first three פסוקים, leaving out 'Do not come close.'
steps.terutzMaskana: Day one: שמות ג:ב–ג; day two: ג:ד; day three: ג:ה, 'Do not come close.'
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The three-day remedy should end with 'Do not come close here.'

steps.title: The final cut of the bush and the fever formula
steps.stepSummary: On the final cut, the person bends low, cuts the bush near the ground, and says a formula. It praises the bush for being humble and asks that the fever flee the sick person, just as fire fled from חנניה, מישאל ועזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when he finishes cutting it, let him bend down low, cut it, and say: 'Bush, bush! It was not because you are taller than all trees that the Holy One, blessed be He, rested His שכינה on you. It was because you are lower than all trees that He rested His שכינה on you. And just as the fire saw חנניה, מישאל ועזריה and ran away from them, so may the fire of this fever see פלוני בר פלונית and run away from him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still describing רבי יוחנן's fever remedy from Steps 2-5. This is the final cut of the bush, and here is the formula the person says while making it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bending low to cut matches the words being said: the bush was chosen because it is low and humble. The fever is called 'fire,' so the formula recalls the fire that could not harm חנניה, מישאל ועזריה. It asks the fever-fire to retreat from the sick person in the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: Because you are low or humble
So-and-so son of so-and-so (his mother). The sick person is named together with his mother's name.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new remedy. It is still the same fever remedy of רבי יוחנן, and this formula goes with the last cut of the bush.

phrases.english: And when he cuts it (the final time),
let him bend down low and cut it,
and say as follows:
'The bush, the bush!
Not because you are taller than all the trees

phrases.aramaic: אַשְׁרִי קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא שְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ עֲלָךְ,
phrases.english: did the Holy One, blessed be He, rest His Divine Presence upon you,
rather, because you are lower than all the trees

phrases.aramaic: אַשְׁרִי קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא שְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ עֲלָךְ.
phrases.english: did the Holy One, blessed be He, rest His Divine Presence upon you.
phrases.notes: The humble bush was chosen, which is why he bends low as he cuts.

phrases.english: And just as the fire saw
Chananya, Mishael, and Azarya
and fled from before them,
so too may the fire (of the fever) see
so-and-so son of so-and-so (his mother)
and flee from before him.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי פָּסֵק לֵיהּ, לִיתַתֵּיהּ וְלִיפְסְקֵיהּ וְלֵימָא הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side question about the order of the פסוקים (Steps 4-5), the גמרא returns to finish describing the remedy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the final cut, bend low, cut the bush, and say the formula about the humble סנה and the fire that fled from חנניה, מישאל ועזריה.

steps.title: A spoken formula for boils
steps.stepSummary: For boils, the person names angels said to have been sent from סדום to heal boils. He then asks the boils to stay as they are, not spread, and not multiply, like a barren creature or a mule.
steps.simpleTranslation: For boils, say: 'Baz, Bazya, Mas, Masya, Kas, Kasya, Sharlai, and Amarlai. These are the angels sent from the land of סדום to heal painful boils. Bazach, Bazich, Bazbazich, Masmasich, Kamon, Kamich. May your appearance stay as it is, may your appearance stay as it is. May your place stay as it is. May your seed be like a barren one and like a mule, which does not reproduce or multiply. So too, do not reproduce or multiply in the body of פלוני בר פלונית.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new item in its list of remedies, a spoken formula for boils.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The formula has two parts. It first names angels connected to healing boils. It then gives commands: the boils should not change color ('your appearance stay with you'), should not spread ('your place stay with you'), and should not multiply, just as a mule cannot reproduce.

keyTerms.meaning: May your appearance stay with you (don't get redder)
May your place stay with you (don't spread)

phrases.english: For boils, let him say as follows:
'Baz, Bazya, Mas, Masya,
Kas, Kasya, Sharlai, and Amarlai,
these are the angels who were sent
from the land of Sodom
and to heal painful boils.
Bazach, Bazich, Bazbazich, Masmasich,
Kamon, Kamich,
may your appearance stay with you, may your appearance stay with you,
phrases.notes: The boils should not grow redder.

phrases.english: may your place stay with you,
may your seed be like a barren one
and like a mule that does not reproduce or multiply,
so too, do not reproduce and do not multiply
in the body of so-and-so son of so-and-so.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The fever remedy is finished, so the list moves on to the next ailment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For boils, say the formula naming the healing angels and commanding the boils not to change, spread, or multiply.

steps.title: A short formula for a wound
steps.stepSummary: For a wound, the person says a short formula that calls up a drawn sword and a ready sling. He declares that the wound should not be ache, sickness, or pain.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a wound, say: 'A drawn sword and a ready sling! Its name shall not be ache, sickness, or pains.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more item to its list, a very short formula for healing a wound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words picture weapons standing ready to fight off the pain. The formula then declares that the wound will not be called pain or sickness, meaning it should not hurt or get worse.

phrases.english: For a wound, let him say as follows:
'A drawn sword and a readied sling,
its name shall not be ache,
sickness, or pains.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next ailment in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a wound, say the formula of the drawn sword and the readied sling.

steps.title: A formula against a demon
steps.stepSummary: To be protected from a demon, the person says it is blocked. He then curses it as broken and banned, calling it by its names.
steps.simpleTranslation: Against a demon, say: 'You were blocked, blocked you were. Cursed, broken, and banned be bar Tit, bar Tamei, bar Tina, as Shamgaz, Merigaz, and Istemai.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another formula in its list, this one for protection from a demon (שד). One more demon formula follows in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repeating 'you were blocked' in both directions stresses that the demon cannot get through. The demon is then cursed and banned by its names, the way a person can be placed in נידוי.

phrases.english: For a demon, let him say as follows:
'You were stopped up, stopped up you were,
cursed, broken, and excommunicated

phrases.aramaic: בַּר טִיט בַּר טָמֵא בַּר טִינָא,
phrases.english: be bar Tit, bar Tamei, bar Tina,
as Shamgaz, Merigaz, and Istemai.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next item in the same list of formulas.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Against a demon, say the formula declaring it blocked and cursing it by name.

steps.title: A formula against the demon of the bathroom
steps.stepSummary: The last formula in the series protects a person from the demon that lives in the bathroom.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the demon of the bathroom, a person should say: 'On the head of a lion and on the nose of a lioness we found the demon bar Shirika Panda. With a bed of leeks I knocked him down, and with the jaw of a donkey I struck him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more protective formula. This one is against the demon believed to live in the bathroom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the formulas in Steps 6 through 9, this is a fixed set of words to say aloud. It names the demon and describes it being caught and beaten. The idea is that announcing the demon's defeat drives it away.
steps.whatToRemember: This closes the list of remedies. רבי יוחנן's fever remedy ends with the humble סנה and the fire that fled (Step 6). Then come four spoken formulas: for boils, for a wound, against a demon, and against the bathroom demon (Steps 7 through 10). From here the גמרא returns to explaining the משנה.

phrases.english: For the demon of the bathroom,
let him say as follows:
"On the head of a lion
and on the nose of a lioness
we found the demon bar Shirika Panda.
With a bed of leeks I knocked him down,
with the jaw of a donkey I struck him."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and completes the list of protective formulas.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Against the bathroom demon, a person says a formula describing the demon caught and beaten.

steps.title: Who taught that princes may go out with bells?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the earlier משנה about princes and bells and asks whose opinion it reflects.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And princes may go out with bells.' Which תנא holds this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to an earlier line of the משנה. That line says princes, and in fact everyone, may go out on שבת with bells. The גמרא asks which תנא holds this, which sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we worry that a person might take off a fancy ornament to show it to others and then carry it in the street. So the גמרא wants to know who allows everyone to wear bells on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: who is the תנא (author) of this teaching?

phrases.english: "And princes with bells."
Who is the tanna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the formulas and returns to explaining the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא allows every person, not only princes, to go out with bells on שבת?

steps.title: It is רבי שמעון, who says all Israel are princes
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא says the משנה follows רבי שמעון, who considers every Jew a prince.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא said: It is רבי שמעון, who said: All Israel are princes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אושעיא answers that this משנה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that every Jew has the status of a prince. Fancy ornaments therefore suit everyone. No one will take them off to show them off, and no one will remove them out of fear of looking pretentious, so there is no fear of carrying.

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya said:
It is Rabbi Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: כׇּל יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּנֵי מְלָכִים הֵם.
phrases.english: who said: All of Israel are princes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי שמעון, who holds that every Jew is a prince, so bells are fitting for everyone.

steps.title: רבא: the bell is woven into the garment, so everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the משנה is talking about bells woven into the clothing, so all תנאים would allow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The case is where the bell is woven into his garment, and so it is the opinion of everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer. The משנה does not need to follow רבי שמעון alone, because it describes bells that are woven into the garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woven-in bell is part of the clothing, so no one can easily take it off and carry it. The worry about removing it is gone. Because of that, every תנא would agree.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not argue with what רבי שמעון holds. He only shows that the משנה can fit every opinion, so it does not have to be limited to רבי שמעון.
steps.whatToRemember: Two ways to explain 'princes with bells': רבי אושעיא says it follows רבי שמעון (all Jews are princes). רבא says the bells are woven in, so everyone agrees.

phrases.english: Rava said:
where it is woven into his garment,
and it is the statement of all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to Step 11 that differs from רבי אושעיא's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The bells are woven into the garment, so there is no fear of removing them, and all תנאים agree.

steps.title: New משנה: going out with healing charms
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר allows going out on שבת with a locust egg, a fox tooth, or a nail from the crucified as a cure. חכמים forbid them even on weekdays as דרכי האמורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may go out on שבת with a locust egg, a fox tooth, and a nail from a crucified person, for healing. These are the words of רבי מאיר. חכמים forbid them even on a weekday, because of דרכי האמורי.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists three charms people wore for healing and records a מחלוקת about them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר treats these as real cures, so wearing them counts like wearing clothing and not like carrying. חכמים see them as superstitious non-Jewish practices. They forbid them every day of the week, not only on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: a nail from a crucified person
'ways of the Amorite', forbidden superstitious non-Jewish practices

steps.confusionAlert: חכמים are not making a שבת rule here. They forbid these charms even on a weekday, because the problem is idolatrous superstition, not carrying.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One may go out with a locust egg
and with a fox tooth
and with a nail from the crucified,
for the purpose of healing
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages forbid even on a weekday,
because of the ways of the Amorite.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹצְאִין בְּבֵיצַת הַחַרְגּוֹל וּבְשֵׁן שׁוּעָל וּבְמַסְמֵר מִן הַצָּלוּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה after the discussion of the previous one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר permits these healing charms on שבת. חכמים forbid them at all times because of דרכי האמורי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is a key source for the איסור of דרכי האמורי. It also raises the question of when a folk remedy counts as real healing rather than superstition.

steps.title: What each charm was used for
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the use of each charm: the locust egg for earache, the fox tooth for sleep problems, and the nail for infection.
steps.simpleTranslation: A locust egg is used for earache. A fox tooth is used for sleep: the tooth of a live fox for someone who sleeps too much, and the tooth of a dead fox for someone who cannot sleep. A nail from the crucified is used for infection.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes through the משנה's list and explains which illness each charm was meant to treat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item is matched to a specific illness, which shows these were treated as cures. The fox tooth has two versions. A live fox's tooth wakes a person who oversleeps, and a dead fox's tooth helps a person who cannot sleep.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the fox teeth. The tooth of the live fox is for the person who sleeps too much, not for the person who cannot sleep.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
"One may go out with a locust egg"
because they use it for earache.
"And with a fox tooth"
because they use it for sleep.
That of a live fox is for one who sleeps too much.
That of a dead fox is for one who does not sleep.
"And with a nail from the crucified"
because they use it for infection.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains each item listed in the משנה of Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Locust egg for earache. Fox tooth for sleep (live fox for oversleeping, dead fox for sleeplessness). Nail from the crucified for infection.

steps.title: אביי and רבא: real healing is not an Amorite practice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites the משנה's words 'for healing — the words of רבי מאיר'. אביי and רבא then rule that anything with real healing value is not forbidden as דרכי האמורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said these charms are allowed 'for healing', according to רבי מאיר. אביי and רבא both said: anything that has real healing value is not considered 'the ways of the Amorite'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points back to a phrase in the משנה and attaches a general rule from אביי and רבא. If something truly heals, it is not a forbidden pagan practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים had called these charms דרכי האמורי, meaning copying pagan superstition. אביי and רבא draw a clear line: if a practice works as medicine, it is not superstition. This rule sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Ways of the Amorite', meaning forbidden pagan or superstitious practices

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic test for when an unusual remedy is allowed: does it actually heal?

phrases.english: [The Mishnah said:] 'for the purpose of healing' — the words of Rabbi Meir.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה that introduces the discussion below.

phrases.english: Abaye and Rava, who both said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם רְפוּאָה
phrases.english: Anything that has an element of healing
does not have the problem of 'the ways of the Amorite.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the dispute in the משנה about charms and gives a general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anything that truly heals is not forbidden as דרכי האמורי.

steps.title: Challenge from painting a tree red
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that something with no healing value would be דרכי האמורי. It challenges this from a ברייתא that allows painting a fruit-dropping tree red, which seems to heal nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does that mean that something without healing value is a forbidden Amorite practice? But a ברייתא teaches: if a tree drops its fruit too early, you may paint it red and load it with stones. Loading it with stones makes sense, because it weakens the tree's excess strength. But what healing does painting it red do?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the reverse side of אביי and רבא's rule. A ברייתא allows painting a tree red, even though it seems to do nothing medically.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only real healing escapes the label דרכי האמורי, then a useless act should be forbidden. The stones have a physical purpose, since they weaken a tree that blossoms too much. The red paint has no clear purpose, yet the ברייתא allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: But was it not taught in a ברייתא? (opens a challenge)
A tree that drops its fruit too early
It makes sense regarding... (grants one part before challenging another)

phrases.english: Does it follow that if it has no element of healing
it does have the problem of 'the ways of the Amorite'?
But was it not taught in a baraita:
A tree that drops its fruit too early —
one marks it and colors it with red paint
and loads it with stones.
It makes sense that he loads it with stones,
so that its strength will be weakened.
phrases.notes: Too much blossoming drains the tree, so weakening it helps it keep its fruit.

phrases.english: But painting it with red paint —
what healing is he doing?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אֵין בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם רְפוּאָה יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם דַּרְכֵי הָאֱמוֹרִי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what follows from אביי and רבא's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication of אביי and רבא's rule: whatever lacks healing value is דרכי האמורי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא allows painting a tree red, an act with no visible healing purpose, so something without healing value is apparently still allowed.

steps.title: The red paint gets people to pray
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the red paint marks the tree so that people will notice it and pray for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is so that people will see the tree and pray for mercy for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The red paint does have a purpose: it draws attention so that people will pray for the tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The red paint is not a physical cure, but it is still a real way of helping, because it brings prayer. So it falls under the healing side of אביי and רבא's rule and is not a superstition.

keyTerms.meaning: Mercy, here meaning prayer for mercy

phrases.english: So that people will see it
and pray for mercy for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about the red paint.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the act: it has a real purpose, getting people to pray.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Painting a tree red seemed purposeless, which would make it like superstition.
steps.terutzMaskana: The paint publicizes the tree's problem so people pray, which counts as a real benefit.

steps.title: Proof from the מצורע calling 'טמא טמא'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its answer with a ברייתא: a מצורע calls out 'טמא טמא' so that people will know his pain and pray for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches on the verse 'And he shall call out: Impure, impure': a person must make his pain known to the public, so that the public will pray for mercy for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source showing that the תורה itself values making a problem public so others will pray.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצורע announces his condition partly to warn people away from טומאה, and also, as this ברייתא explains, so that many people will pray for him. This shows that publicizing a problem to bring prayer is a real idea approved by the תורה, just like the red paint on the tree.

keyTerms.meaning: As was taught in a ברייתא (introduces support)
To make his pain known to the public

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice of telling others about an illness or trouble so they will pray.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
'And he shall call out: Impure, impure' (Leviticus 13:45).
He must make his pain known to the public,
and the public will pray for mercy for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer that publicizing a problem brings prayer.
steps.raayaObject: That marking something so others will pray is a real, legitimate purpose.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on the מצורע calling 'טמא טמא' (ויקרא 13:45).

steps.title: רבינא: hanging date clusters on a palm follows this view
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the custom of hanging date clusters on a palm tree that drops its fruit follows this תנא, who teaches that one should publicize pain so others will pray.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Whose view do we follow when we hang clusters of dates on a palm tree? The view of this תנא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא connects a practice of his own time to the idea just taught. Hanging dates on a struggling palm tree publicizes its problem so people will pray.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The date clusters work like the red paint: they are a visible sign that the tree is in trouble. Because the purpose is to bring prayer, the practice is allowed and is not דרכי האמורי.
steps.whatToRemember: A practice is not דרכי האמורי if it truly heals, and getting people to pray, as with the red-painted tree, the מצורע, and the date clusters, counts as real help.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
According to whom do we hang clusters of dates on a palm tree?
According to this tanna.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: כְּמַאן תָּלֵינַן כּוּבְסֵי בְּדִיקְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the principle from the ברייתא to a practice in רבינא's time.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hanging date clusters on a struggling palm tree is allowed, because it follows the תנא who says one should publicize pain so others will pray.

steps.title: Almost everything in the Amorite chapter is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites the chapter of Amorite practices before רבי חייא בר אבין. He responds that all of them are forbidden as דרכי האמורי, except for a few he is about to list.
steps.simpleTranslation: A reciter taught the 'Amorite chapter' in front of רבי חייא בר אבין. He told him: all of these practices are forbidden because they are Amorite ways, except for the following ones.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבין gives a general rule: every practice in the 'Amorite chapter' is forbidden. This step sets up the next move, a short list of exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a whole collection of ברייתות listing forbidden superstitious practices. רבי חייא בר אבין confirms the list as forbidden but says a few items are allowed. The words 'לבר מהני' ('except for these') tell us a list of permitted items is coming.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: a professional reciter who memorized ברייתות and recited them before the אמוראים
The 'chapter of the Amorites', a collection of ברייתות listing superstitious practices
'Ways of the Amorite': forbidden superstitious practices of the nations

steps.confusionAlert: The word תנא here does not mean a sage from the time of the משנה. It means a 'reciter', a person whose job was to memorize ברייתות and recite them in the בית מדרש.

phrases.english: A reciter taught the chapter of the Amorites
phrases.notes: The section of ברייתות that lists Amorite practices

phrases.english: before Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Avin.
He said to him: All of them contain
the prohibition of the ways of the Amorite,
except for these:

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא בְּפֶרֶק אֱמוֹרָאֵי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the discussion of which practices count as healing to a general statement about the whole Amorite chapter, which sets up a list of exceptions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All practices in the Amorite chapter are forbidden as דרכי האמורי, except for a specific list.

steps.title: Remedy for a bone stuck in the throat
steps.stepSummary: The first exception: a person with a bone stuck in his throat places a bone of the same kind on his head and says a short formula. This is not דרכי האמורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone has a bone stuck in his throat, he takes a bone from the same kind of animal, puts it on top of his head, and says: 'One by one, go down, be swallowed; be swallowed, go down, one by one.' This is not forbidden as an Amorite practice.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבין gives the first permitted practice, a remedy for a bone stuck in the throat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The remedy uses an action (a matching bone on the head) and a spoken formula. Even though it looks like a superstition, it is allowed. This fits the earlier rule from אביי and רבא that anything with healing value is not דרכי האמורי.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a practice which looks magical can still be permitted when it is understood as a cure. This matches the principle in Step 16.

phrases.english: One who has a bone in his throat
brings a bone from the same species
and places it on his skull,
and let him say as follows:
'One by one, go down, be swallowed,
be swallowed, go down, one by one,'
it does not contain the prohibition of the ways of the Amorite.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ עֶצֶם בִּגְרוֹנוֹ מֵבִיא מֵאוֹתוֹ הַמִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first item in the list of exceptions announced in Step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Placing a same-kind bone on the head and saying the formula for a stuck bone is permitted, not דרכי האמורי.

steps.title: Formula for a stuck fish bone
steps.stepSummary: For a fish bone stuck in the throat, a different formula is said. It continues the list of permitted practices.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a fish bone, he should say: 'You are stuck like a needle, locked like a shield; go down, go down.'
steps.whatsHappening: The list of exceptions continues with a special formula to say when a fish bone is stuck in the throat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fish bone is thin and sharp, so it gets its own wording: it is described as stuck like a needle and blocking like a shield. Like the previous remedy, this is a permitted exception to דרכי האמורי.

keyTerms.meaning: A shield (also explained as a shutter)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חייא בר אבין says the whole Amorite chapter is forbidden, with exceptions. The first exceptions are throat remedies: a same-kind bone on the head with a formula, and a special formula for a fish bone.

phrases.english: For a fish bone, let him say as follows:
'You are stuck like a needle,
locked as a shield,
go down, go down.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second throat remedy, specific to fish bones, to the list of exceptions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying this formula for a stuck fish bone is permitted, not דרכי האמורי.
